page: Microsoft Azure FX12-6mds_v2 is a compute and memory intensive virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, providing 6 vCPUs across 3 physical cores with 2 threads per core on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512 extensions, AMX tile and int8 matrices, and cryptographic acceleration. Cache resources feature 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache.

A key characteristic of this configuration is its high memory-to-vCPU ratio, provisioning 252.0 GB of total RAM, or 42.0 GB per vCPU. In addition to high-capacity system memory, the instance bundles 945 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The server does not include GPU accelerators and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded compute efficiency driven by the 4.2 GHz clock rate. Geekbench single-core testing reached 2357.0 points (top 10%), paired with top-tier text processing performance at 2951.0 points and top-quartile gzip compression at 34.96 GB/sec. Multi-core compute metrics reflect the lower core count, scoring 7305.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 12021.43 in PassMark CPU tests. Redis operations reached 9.46 million SET operations per second, while uncached memory read bandwidth registered at 51.24 GB/sec.

The balance of constrained vCPU count paired with 252.0 GB RAM and fast NVMe storage presents favorable resource density for memory-bound applications that require high single-thread clock speeds without paying for unneeded vCPUs. Tradeoffs include limited multi-threaded throughput and modest large-model CPU inference capabilities. FX12-6mds_v2 is well configured for in-memory caches, relational database workloads, financial modeling, and memory-constrained data analysis.
